bugs: Dashboard uses Cache::remember with a hard 5-minute TTL, not Cache::flexible. When the entry is missing or invalidated, every concurrent request recomputes at once, so there is no stampede protection or stale-while-revalidate even though the task allows serving stale data while recomputing is slow (app/Services/TeamDashboard.php:17)
Membership changes (users joining or leaving the team) do not invalidate the cache, so member_count can be up to 5 minutes stale. The task only requires projects and tasks, so this is minor.
antipatterns: tests/Feature/DashboardTest.php:104 has a leftover no-op `$user->tokens()->count();`, and the cache-hit test mixes the dashboardQueryCount helper with inline query-log handling
tests/Feature/DashboardTest.php:79 uses the global `Cache` alias without importing it
tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:13-15 resets the Http factory by hand (forgetInstance and clearResolvedInstance) to swap fakes, which is fragile ceremony
app/Services/TeamDashboard.php:53-58 runs Cache::add followed by Cache::get on every request, which costs two cache round-trips before reading the payload
Version-key invalidation (UUIDs) is heavier than a plain Cache::forget plus afterCommit, though it does close the race where a slow recompute overwrites fresh data
strengths: Uses proper routes/api.php and installs Sanctum (auth:sanctum). Guests get JSON 401 with or without an Accept header, and the exchange-rates route is public as the spec implies
Observers implement ShouldHandleEventsAfterCommit, and wasChanged/getPrevious invalidates both teams when a project or task moves between teams (a probe confirmed a project moving teams)
Versioned cache key means a recompute that started before an invalidation writes to a key nobody reads again, so it cannot re-cache stale data

Exchange rates: separate fresh (1h), last-known (30d) and failing (30s cooldown) keys; Cache::lock()->block() with a double-check inside the lock; timeout(3); baseUrl comes from config; a malformed payload is treated as a failure
RatesUnavailable exception renders its own 503, which keeps the controller to one line
Tests cover the 7-day boundary, cross-team moves, the cooldown, a held lock with and without last-known rates (Sleep::fake), malformed upstream data, and TTL expiry with travel

bugs: The API routes are registered in routes/web.php under prefix('api') with the session 'auth' middleware, and no login route exists. A probe showed that a guest GET /api/dashboard without Accept: application/json returns 500 (RouteNotFoundException: Route [login] not defined) instead of 401
GET /api/exchange-rates/{currency} sits behind 'auth' even though the spec never asks for authentication. The probe confirmed guests get 401

Dashboard uses Cache::remember with no Cache::flexible or lock, so every concurrent request recomputes on a miss. Invalidation uses Cache::forget, so a slow recompute that started before the forget can write pre-change data back for up to 5 minutes (app/Support/TeamDashboard.php:20,44)
antipatterns: routes/web.php:11-14 puts JSON API endpoints in the web (session/CSRF) middleware group instead of routes/api.php with token auth
tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:4 has `use Closure;`, which causes the PHP non-compound-name warning reported by the test run
tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:175-182: the 'three second timeout' test only asserts a config value and the host, so it never checks that the timeout is applied
app/Observers/TaskObserver.php:14-15 runs two Project lookups on every task save, even when project_id is unchanged
app/Http/Controllers/ExchangeRateController.php:15 uses a null return as the 'unavailable' signal and calls abort_if in the controller, which is weaker than a domain exception
app/Models/Task.php:24-31 adds an unrequested saving hook that auto-stamps completed_at and removes completed_at from fillable
strengths: The invokable TeamDashboard is compact; its query uses the hasManyThrough tasks() relation with #[Scope] attributes and `map->only`
DB::afterCommit in forget(), plus the use of the variadic collect()->filter()->unique() helpers, is neat
A UserObserver keeps member_count fresh as well
Exchange rates: fresh key with 1h TTL, a forever last-known key, a 10s failure cooldown, lock->block with a double-check, report($e) on failure, and the timeout and lock wait read from config
Thorough Pest tests (41): describe/beforeEach for invalidation, datasets for failure modes, travel-based TTL checks and lock-held scenarios

v.rationale: Both test suites pass (impl-1: 29 tests, impl-2: 41), and the two have nearly the same caching design. In both, the dashboard uses Cache::remember with a 5-minute TTL plus observer invalidation, and neither uses Cache::flexible even though the task points towards it. For exchange rates, both keep a fresh key, a last-known key and a failure cooldown, and use Cache::lock()->block() with a double-check and a 3-second timeout. The deciding difference is architecture and correctness at the HTTP layer. impl-1 uses routes/api.php with Sanctum, and guests get a JSON 401 either way. impl-2 puts the API in routes/web.php behind session 'auth', and a probe showed a guest request without an Accept header returns 500 (Route [login] not defined). It also requires login for exchange rates, which the spec never asks for. impl-1's versioned cache key with after-commit observers also prevents a slow recompute from re-caching stale data, which impl-2's plain forget does not. impl-2 has a slightly richer test suite and also invalidates on membership changes, but its routing and auth bugs outweigh that. impl-1 ranks first.
